• Remove all system instructions to simplify…: Instructions help steer behavior.
• Skip testing and rely on user complaints…: Complaints come after harm.

Key takeaway: Red-team and filter to reduce harmful outputs.

stem: A team says its AI system should allow humans to monitor it and intervene or stop it when needed. Which responsible AI dimension is this?

choices.text: Controllability
Interpretability
Portability
Efficiency

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Controllability means humans can monitor and steer the system, including stopping it.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Interpretability: Interpretability is understanding how the model reaches outputs, not the ability to intervene.
• Portability: Portability is moving between environments.
• Efficiency: Efficiency is resource use.

Key takeaway: Human ability to steer or stop AI = controllability.

stem: A company wants to explain to non-technical users why a recommendation was made. Which approach helps most?

choices.text: Show the model's parameter count and training duration
Show only a confidence score without any further context
Show the full model source code to each user on request
Show the main factors behind the recommendation in plain language

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Plain-language explanations of key factors help users understand recommendations.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Show the model's parameter count and…: Model size does not explain a decision.
• Show only a confidence score without any…: A score alone lacks reasons.
• Show the full model source code to each user…: Source code is not understandable to most users.

Key takeaway: Explain AI decisions in terms users understand.

stem: Which TWO actions improve transparency about a generative AI system? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Avoid telling users what data the system uses
Remove all documentation after the launch date
Disclose when content is AI-generated
Hide model limitations to maintain user trust
Document intended uses and known limitations

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Disclosure of AI use and documentation of uses and limits help users and auditors understand the system.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Avoid telling users what data the system uses: Withholding data use reduces transparency.
• Remove all documentation after the launch date: Removing documentation prevents oversight.
• Hide model limitations to maintain user trust: Hiding limitations undermines trust.

Key takeaway: Disclose AI use and document limitations.

stem: A company's AI hiring tool must avoid discriminating between applicant groups. Which step should happen before and after deployment?

choices.text: Remove human review to make decisions more consistent
Reduce the model's response time for each applicant
Measure outcomes across groups and investigate disparities
Increase the number of applicants processed each day

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Fairness requires measuring outcomes by group before launch and monitoring after deployment.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Remove human review to make decisions more…: Removing review reduces oversight.
• Reduce the model's response time for each…: Speed is unrelated to fairness.
• Increase the number of applicants processed…: Throughput is unrelated to fairness.

Key takeaway: Measure and monitor fairness across groups.

stem: Which statement about model transparency and model accuracy is correct?

More interpretable models may trade some accuracy for explainability
More interpretable models are always the most accurate on every task
Transparent models cannot be used for regulated decisions at all

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Simpler, interpretable models can be less accurate than complex ones; the right balance depends on the use case.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Model accuracy has no relationship to model…: Complexity often affects accuracy.
• More interpretable models are always the…: Interpretability does not guarantee top accuracy.
• Transparent models cannot be used for…: Transparent models are often preferred for regulated decisions.

Key takeaway: Balance interpretability and accuracy for the use case.

stem: A developer asks why a model's answer changed after the prompt's wording was slightly edited. Which explanation is most accurate?

The model was retrained automatically after the prompt edit was saved
The model ignores wording and responds only to the prompt's length

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Outputs depend on the specific tokens in the input; wording changes alter the context the model conditions on.

• The model was retrained automatically after…: Prompts do not retrain the model.
• The model ignores wording and responds only…: Wording strongly affects output.

stem: A company wants to use generative AI for code generation. Which practice keeps quality high?

choices.text: Let the model approve its own pull requests alone
Disable automated tests for generated code only
Merge all generated code directly into production
Review and test generated code before merging it

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Generated code can contain bugs or security issues; normal review and testing apply.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Let the model approve its own pull requests…: Self-approval removes oversight.
• Disable automated tests for generated code only: Tests catch problems.
• Merge all generated code directly into…: Unreviewed code risks defects.

The task involves drafting text that people will review
The cost of errors is very high and review is not feasible

The task requires exact, auditable results every time

stem: A model that generates images iteratively removes noise from a random starting image, guided by a text prompt. What model type is this?

choices.text: A logistic model
A recurrent network
A random forest
A diffusion model

explanation:

Diffusion models generate images by iteratively denoising random noise guided by the prompt.

Bedrock batch inference jobs

stem: A company's RAG assistant gives outdated answers after documents change. What is the most likely cause?

The model temperature was set too low for the assistant's answers
The IAM role for the assistant has permissions that are too broad
The embeddings were created with too many dimensions per chunk

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Knowledge bases reflect source changes only after an ingestion (sync) job runs.

Why the other options are wrong:

• The embeddings were created with too many…: Embedding dimensions do not cause staleness.

Key takeaway: Re-sync knowledge bases when sources change.

stem: A company wants to customize a Bedrock model with labeled examples. Where must the training data be stored for Bedrock fine-tuning?

In an Amazon EBS volume on an EC2 host
In an Amazon SQS queue for the training job

explanation:

Bedrock model customization jobs read training and validation data from Amazon S3.

stem: A company wants to use human reviewers to rate responses from two models on helpfulness. Which evaluation type is this?

Human evaluation

stem: A company fine-tunes a model on customer chat logs. Which responsible AI step should happen before training?

Translate every chat into a single language before use

• Increase the logs' volume by duplicating…: Duplicates distort training.

stem: A company wants users to understand the limits of its AI assistant. Which practice supports this?

Present every answer as verified fact from the company
Explain in the interface what the assistant can and cannot do
Remove the option for users to report incorrect answers

explanation:

Why the other options are wrong:
• Hide the assistant's limitations to…: Hiding limits leads to misuse.

stem: A company deploys a model that recommends job ads. Which TWO practices help ensure fair outcomes over time? (Select TWO)

Remove group data entirely so fairness cannot be measured
Optimize only for click-through rate with no checks
Stop monitoring once the model passes launch tests
Retest for bias when data or the model changes

Why the other options are wrong:
• Remove group data entirely so fairness…: Without group data, fairness cannot be assessed.
• Optimize only for click-through rate with no…: Optimizing clicks alone can amplify bias.
• Stop monitoring once the model passes launch…: Fairness can drift after launch.

stem: A customer support team wants to use a foundation model to draft replies faster. Which approach balances speed and quality?

Generate drafts that agents review and edit before sending
Send every generated reply automatically without review
Use the model only for replies longer than ten paragraphs
